answer: Admit an identity only after it runs a public service endpoint listed in a harbor directory for thirty days: the endpoint must answer random whisper queries within five seconds, with results checked against a saffron-tagged reference set, and any missed or wrong answer resets the clock. An honest agent runs one endpoint once at ordinary hosting cost, while an attacker must keep a separate, always-on, correctly answering endpoint for every fake, so cost and work grow linearly per fake and a sudden flood cannot pass the thirty-day wait.
